body.p: The Office Action of March 6, 2023 has been carefully reviewed. The Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider the rejections and allow the pending claims in view of the following remarks.
Claims 1-30 are pending.
Claims 3-4 and 7-8 are canceled.
Claims 1, 2, 5, 9-11, 16, 19-21, 25-27, 29, and 30 are hereby amended.
New claims 31-34 are added herein.
Claims 1, 2, 5, 6, and 9-34 are now pending in this application.

The Applicant thanks Examiner Jackson and Primary Examiner Jen for participating in the telephone interview with the Applicant's representative Gayatry Nair, Reg. No. 70,812 on May 9,2023. During the interview, the Examiners agreed that the amendments presented herein would overcome the rejection of the independent claims under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) and 35 U.S.C. § 103. However, the Examiners indicated that further search and consideration would be necessary.
Claim 1 is objected to due to informalities. See Office Action, p. 2. Specifically, the Office Action states that claim 1 should be amended to recite "objects being within reach..." See id. Claim
1 has been amended according to the suggestion in the Office Action. Accordingly, the Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to withdraw the objection to claim 1.
Claims 1, 3-7, 10-11, 15-19, 21, and 29 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0133689 to Johnson, et al. ("Johnson").

As mentioned above, the Examiners agreed during the interview that independent claims 1, 19, and 29 as amended are allowable over Johnson. Claims 3-7, 10-11, 15-18, and 21 depend from independent claims 1, 19, and 29, and thus, are also allowable over Johnson.

Claims 2, 8-9, 20, 25-26, and 30 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Johnson in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2020/0405406 to Harris, et al. ("Harris"). Claims 12-14 and 22-24 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Johnson in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0078439 to Cagle, et al. ("Cagle"). Claim 27 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Johnson in view of Harris and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2017/0296277 to Hourtash, et al. ("Hourtash"). Claim 28 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Johnson in view of Harris and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0036884 to Chen, et al.
("Chen").
As mentioned above, the Examiners agreed during the interview that independent claim 25 as amended is allowable over the combination of Johnson and Harris. Claims 26-28 depend from
independent claim 25, and thus, are also allowable over the combination of Johnson and Harris. The addition of Hourtash and/or Chen does not cure the deficiencies of Johnson and Harris.

In addition, claims 2, 8-9, 12-14, 20, 22-24, and 30 depend from either independent claim 1, 19, or 29. As mentioned above, independent claims 1, 19, and 29 as amended are allowable over Johnson. The addition of Harris, Cagle, Hourtash and/or Chen does not cure the deficiencies of Johnson.
Therefore, claims 2, 8-9, 12-14, 20, 22-28, and 30 are allowable over the cited art.

New claims 31-34 recite novel and non-obvious aspects of the disclosure. Support for new claims 31-34 is found in paragraphs 125-127 of the application. Thus, no new matter is contained in these claims. New claims 31-34 depend from claim 1, which is allowable for the reasons stated above. Thus, new claims 31-34 are also allowable.

Consideration of the foregoing amendments and remarks, reconsideration of the application, and withdrawal of the rejections and objections is respectfully requested by the Applicant. No new matter is introduced by way of the amendment. It is believed that each ground of rejection raised in the Office Action dated March 6, 2023 has been fully addressed. If any fee is due as a result of the filing of this paper, please appropriately charge such fee to Deposit Account Number 50-1515 of Conley Rose, P.C., Texas. If a petition for extension of time is necessary in order for this paper to be deemed timely filed, please consider this a petition therefor.

If a telephone conference would facilitate the resolution of any issue or expedite the prosecution of the application, the Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the telephone number given below.
Respectfully submitted,
CONLEY ROSE, P.C.
